 Sasha Jovanovic Thu, 12 November 2026 at 11:10 am GMT-8 4 min read MSFT +0.21% 
 The Ohio State University's Wexner Medical Center is teaming up with Microsoft (MSFT) on a five year AI and cloud partnership that targets clinical care, research workloads, and healthcare workforce training. 
 For investors watching the ticker, Microsoft's recent flurry of AI alliances has landed against a softer tape. The share price is down 4.11% over 30 days but still shows a 5.19% 90 day share price gain and a 10.19% year to date share price return. Total shareholder return sits at 4.40% over one year and builds to 41.49% over three years and 58.82% over five years, suggesting shorter term momentum has cooled even as the longer term compounding story remains intact. 
 See how Microsoft's AI push compares with other potential compounders by lining up its profile against 32 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Bulls point to Microsoft's AI deals and solid recent earnings, while bears focus on rising capex, political risk and new rivals. The numbers and cash generation raise a clear next question: What is the stock worth today? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 24% Overvalued 
 On the most followed view, Microsoft's fair value sits at $419.91, which trails the recent $521.13 close and frames the stock as expensive on that measure. According to CubanEros, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the gap is less about business weakness and more about what investors are willing to pay. 
 Microsoft rarely goes on sale, so it''s worth paying attention when the multiple compresses. At around $380, the stock trades at roughly 22 to 23x trailing earnings and approximately 14x EV/EBITDA, well below its own seven year historical range. This is the cheapest Microsoft has been in years, and the de-rating looks more like a capex cycle worry than a deterioration in the business. 
 See why 297 investors see Microsoft as 24% overvalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of $419.91 (OVERVALUED) 
 Still, the narrative could crack if AI driven capex fails to earn solid returns, or if regulatory pressure hits Microsoft's cloud and OpenAI exposure. 
 Find out about the key risks to this Microsoft narrative . 
 Another View: Microsoft Through Market Ratios 
 That first narrative leans on a detailed fair value estimate. A simpler lens tells a different story. On a P/E of 27.1x, Microsoft trades below the US Software industry at 31.2x and above its peer group on 24.3x, while the fair ratio sits much higher at 56x. For you as an investor, that mix of discount to the sector, premium to peers, and large gap to the fair ratio frames real valuation risk and opportunity. Decide which reference point matters most for your own hurdle rate.
